thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts observed in us-east-1 across gateway-prod cluster. spike started ~12:03 UTC. error-rate ~6.2% (5m), p95 latency 2.2s -> p95 7.1s. paging oncall.

anya (oncall): acked. I'm on it. Paging infra/eng-sre. @eli @maria can you grab triage?

eli: got it. pulling metrics. seeing scheduler queue length 18k, oldest request age ~95s, many stuck batches in 'running' state. looks like one model variant started spawning long-running decode loops.

kevin: which model variant? any recent deploys?

deploy-bot: CI: deploy redwood-gateway/2026.03.14-22 -> prod/us-east-1 completed at 11:58 UTC. no rollbacks.

maria: not a gateway deploy. noise in scheduling: batcher saturation -> head-of-line blocking. some batches are huge token counts, pinning workers. KV cache growth also up 3x.

anya (oncall): customer impact? support-bot, can you surface active customer errors?

support-bot: Affected customers (sample): AcmeCorp (502), Shoplytics (504), internal smoke tests failing. Estimated % of requests affected: ~4-7% depending by route. No billing hit yet but degraded UX.

ops-lucy: I can spin more batchers but want to avoid cascading cache growth. Proposal: 1) enable emergency route-level rate limit for high-cost routes 2) add temporary fallback route to quantized small model 3) restart scheduler pods one-by-one to clear stuck batches.

eli: agreed with lucy. also we should apply a token max on incoming requests for the affected route to prevent monster batches. can do at gateway rewrite layer.

kevin: where's the runbook for batching saturation? linking: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/batching-saturation

anya (oncall): following runbook steps 1-3. I'm going to add a soft rate limit on /v1/chat.generate for customers with >2000 token requests.

anya (oncall): commands I'm running now:
```
# edge rule: limit token param
redwoodctl gateway-rules add --route "/v1/chat.generate" --condition "tokens>2000" --action rate_limit=20/s --reason "emergency HOL mitigation"
kubectl rollout restart deploy/scheduler -n ingress --timeout=5m
```

eli: I'm creating fallback route to redwood-compact-v1 (quantized) and routing 20% of traffic to it as a safety net.

eli: command:
```
redwoodctl routes create --from /v1/chat.generate --to model:redwood-compact-v1 --weight 20 --meta "emergency-fallback"
```

maria: flushing prefix KV cache only for affected shard to avoid global cold start. doing shard 3 now.

ops-lucy: increasing scheduler replicas by +3 for the affected ASG to help drain backlog. watch for spike in network IO.

anya (oncall): applying prioritized preemptive eviction for long-running batches (preempt oldest >60s). See runbook step 4.

kevin: any changes to dedicated pools? customer-facing Dedicated tenants unaffected so far.

maria: no changes to Dedicated. this is scheduler-level on shared pool. we must avoid evicting healthy short jobs.

deploy-bot: NOTE: config change pushed to gateway-rules by anya at 12:11 UTC.

eli: 12:13 - queue length dropping from 18k -> 7.4k. oldest age down to 30s. error-rate trending down: 6.2% -> 2.0%.

support-bot: customer updates posted to status page (automated): https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-03-14-queue-surge

anya (oncall): continuing to monitor. next step: if queue not <1k within 10m, escalate to full scheduler restart which is disruptive. tagging eng-sre for readiness.

maria: preemptive eviction ran, flushed shard, added fallback, and scaled +3. system trending OK. p95 latency now 1.1s, error-rate 0.8%.

ops-lucy: good sign. will leave the emergency rules in place for 30m, then gradually remove. documenting all commands in incident doc.

eli: handing off to night oncall @kevin at 12:22 UTC. kevin, you're the owner for post-incident follow-up and postmortem.

kevin: taking handoff. I'll collect logs, capture the batch IDs, and start a blameless postmortem. timeline so far + runbook steps will go into the incident ticket.

anya (oncall): final checks: verify fallback model output quality for a sample of requests, confirm no data exfiltration flags. maria/eli please confirm.

maria: sampled outputs look reasonable for fallback. no PII flags triggered.

eli: confirm logs saved to s3://redwood-incidents/1730000000/gateway-spillover/ and tracing traces linked in ticket.

kevin: thanks everyone. I'll open the postmortem and assign action items: improve token-size gating at client side, add automatic batch-size caps in scheduler, and alerting on KV cache growth.

support-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Will post final update when postmortem ready. :white_check_mark:

anya (oncall): closing thread for live mitigation. leaving emergency rules for 25m then revert. next steps in ticket #INC-1730. :lock_with_key:
